messages.author: d0cb4305c7d89d16
messages.subject: Model modification (from Mplus to lavaan)
parts:
Dear lavaan community,

I have the following question. In the original article on the factorial structure of the English version of the Post-Concussion Symptom Inventory (PSCI), the model parameters were specified as follows (estimation using Mplus):

„In each model, the factors were allowed to correlate, factor variance was fixed to 1.0, the unstandardized factor loading for the first item on each factor was fixed to 1.0, and residual covariances were fixed to 0.0.“

For the validation of the German version of this questionnaire I would like to use the same specifications. However, I find it difficult to find corresponding parameters and to define them correctly. The initial model (four factors without any further restrictions) is defined as follows:



eight.model <- '

physical =~ pcsisr801 +

pcsisr802 +

pcsisr803 +

pcsisr804 +

pcsisr805 +

pcsisr806 +

pcsisr807 +

pcsisr808



emotional =~ pcsisr809 +

pcsisr810 +

pcsisr811



cognitive =~ pcsisr812 +

pcsisr813 +

pcsisr814 +

pcsisr815



fatigue =~ pcsisr816 +

pcsisr817'

I would like to use the following cfa-function:

fit.pcsi8.fix <- cfa(eight.model, 

                     data = pcsi8,

                     ordered = items.pcsi8)

 

Could you please give me some advice, how to set…

1      …correlated factors (model default unless otherwise specified?)

2      …factor variance to 1

3      …unstandardized factor loading for the first item on each factor to 1 (model default unless otherwise specified?)

4      …residual covariances to 0

 

Should I specify these parameters in the model definition or use cfa-parameters?

 

Thank you and best wishes,

Marina

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Model modification (from Mplus to lavaan)
parts: 1      …correlated factors (model default unless otherwise specified?)
This happens by default in cfa()
2      …factor variance to 1
You can set the argument std.lv=TRUE in your cfa() call.
3      …unstandardized factor loading for the first item on each factor to 1 (model default unless otherwise specified?)
Why would someone do that if the factor variance was already fixed to 1?  It sounds like someone was confused and used 2 different identification constraints, needlessly constraining the model.
4      …residual covariances to 0

The ?model.syntax help page shows how to specify (co)variance parameters in the syntax, but this is also the default setting.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
